 🏏 T20 international updatees at the MCG in Melbourne
 🏏 Play starts at 7.15pm AEDT/8.15am GMT | Send us a mail

 27s ago 06.27 EST WICKET! Australia 168-7 (Chaudhary c Donald b Overton 66)
 Chaudhary blasts Overton over extra cover for two more fours – but then he falls to the final ball of the over! He lifted Overton wristily towards deep square, where Donald took an awkward low catch. Yet another twist in this captivating plot.
 Share 5m ago 06.22 EST 17th over: Australia 156-6 (Chaudhary 57, Edwards 0) That was the last ball of an eventful over: 12 runs, two wickets.
 Share 6m ago 06.22 EST WICKET! Australia 156-6 (Davies c Donald b Jacks 1)
 Chaudhary plays another eye-catching stroke, pulling Jacks over long-on for six. But he may have to win this game off his own bat because they’re dropping like flies at the other end. Jack Davies has fallen to a poor stroke; instead of supporting Chaudhary, he lifted Jacks recklessly over the leg side and was comfortably caught by Donald running in from deep midwicket.
 Share 9m ago 06.19 EST WICKET! Australia 148-5 (Shaw c Rashid b Jacks 5)
 Another twist in this ding-dong contest. Shaw reverse sweeps Jacks confidently for four but then gives a simple catch to Rashid in the covers. Australia need 40 from 22 balls. I don’t know who’s favourite. 
 Share 11m ago 06.16 EST 16th over: Australia 144-4 (Chaudhary 50, Shaw 1) The new batter is the debutant Lachlan Shaw.
 Rashid finishes a good spell with identical figures to Dawson: 4-0-30-1.
 Share 12m ago 06.15 EST WICKET! Australia 143-4 (David c Overton b Rashid 20)
 Chaudhary drags Rashid back onto off stump – but the bails stay on and so his innings continues. He pushes the next ball for a single to reach a classy fifty , his first in international cricket, from 32 balls.
 I’ve no idea how the bails stayed on because the ball hit the stumps with a fair bit of force.
 England do get a wicket, perhaps a more important one, when David belabours Rashid into the bucket hands of Overton at log-on. They really need that. Australia need 45 from 25 balls.
 View image in fullscreen A disappointed Tim David exits. Photograph: James Ross/AAP Share Updated at  06.23 EST 17m ago 06.11 EST 15th over: Australia 136-3 (Chaudhary 44, David 19) Curran returns and exchanges a few unpleasantries with Chaudhary, who has taken England on with bat, ball and mouth. Right now it looks like Australia are going to have the final word. An otherwise excellent over from Curran is tarnished when David pulls his final ball round the corner for four.
 Share 21m ago 06.06 EST 14th over: Australia 127-3 (Chaudhary 42, David 12) Ah, there he is. After taking precisely six balls to get his eye in, Tim David rocket-launches Dawson back over his head for a 113-metre six .
 The usual singles keep Australia on track. Dawson ends a decent night’s work with figures of 4-0-30-1. England need wickets, quicksmart.
 View image in fullscreen Tim David hits out. Photograph: Morgan Hancock/CA/Cricket Australia/Getty Images Share Updated at  06.08 EST 26m ago 06.02 EST 13th over: Australia 116-3 (Chaudhary 40, David 4) Jamie Overton, aka Big Overs, returns after conceding 21 from his only over to date. He starts well, three from the first four balls, but then Chaudhary plays a remarkable one-handed ramp for six . He was beaten for pace, bounce or both but improved to play a kind of self-defence swat that flew over his shoulder and went all the way. Chaudhary is having a helluvan all-round game.
 “Interesting that they’ve made that decision about Warner and Khawaja, particularly as I woke this morning and stuck on the radio to be greeted by the dulcet tones of Darren Lehmann on ABC,” says Phil Harrison. “He doesn’t seem to be being taken off air so clearly sides have been picked and ranks are being closed.”
 Do you think sides are being picked? I haven’t had time to think it through but it feels like two different broadcasters reaching independent decisions. (And it wouldn’t surprise me if Lehmann takes a break at some stage.)
 Share 32m ago 05.56 EST 12th over: Australia 105-3 (Chaudhary 31, David 2) The impressive Chaudhary clubs Rashid to long-off for four, just beating the diving Banton. That’s the first boundary Rashid has conceded in his three overs (I think). The usual ones and twos make it 10 from the over, which will do Australia nicely. They need 84 from 48 balls. 
 “Hi Rob,” says Tim Woods. “Glad you’re feeling better. Not that I stalk my favourite Guardian writers but your temporary absence was noted and you were missed! I’m currently in Harare, where there is very little evidence of the cricket being followed, football very much number one. I even saw a minibus dedicated to Patrick Dorgu, which isn’t something you spot every day. Probably not even in Salford.”
 In fairness, I’d be happy if a Sinclair C5 was dedicated to me, never mind a minibus.
 Share 35m ago 05.53 EST 11th over: Australia 95-3 (Chaudhary 23, David 0) Dawson’s catch was made even better by the fact the ball was tight to his chest, so he couldn’t reach out fully to grab it. Quite brilliant.
 Share 36m ago 05.51 EST WICKET! Australia 95-3 (Marsh c Dawson b Curran 37)
 Marsh waits for Sam Curran’s moon ball, waits another split-second and then launches it over mid-off for four. But that’s all she wrote: he pulls Curran’s last ball ferociously towards short fine leg, where Dawson takes a sensational two-handed catch in mid-air. Pick that out! (Yes, he did.)
 View image in fullscreen Liam Dawson is congratulated by Jordan Cox after sensationally catching out Mitchell Marsh. Photograph: Asanka Brendon Ratnayake/AP Share Updated at  06.00 EST 41m ago 05.47 EST 10th over: Australia 86-2 (Marsh 32, Chaudhary 18) Chaudhary chips Rashid gracefully over extra cover, this time for two rather than four. Eight from the over, none in boundaries. Australia need 102 from 60 balls and don’t you dare ask me who are favourites to win.
 Share 43m ago 05.45 EST Warner and Khawaja taken off air
 Sandpaper never sleeps. Here’s the latest development, taken from the AFP news wires.
 double quotation mark Usman Khawaja and David Warner were taken off television commentary duties on Saturday until the “Sandpapergate” storm passes, with both set to miss Australia’s entire Twenty20 series against England.
 The retired pair have been the centre of attention since Khawaja claimed in his autobiography more than two weeks ago that the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball in a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.
 Only then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft – who used the sandpaper – were found to be responsible by a Cricket Australia probe.
 The move by Fox Sports, for whom they both work, came after Cricket Australia threw its “unanimous support” behind embattled Test captain Pat Cummins.
 Cummins denied he knew what was going on and has been under huge pressure since Khawaja’s claims, which were first backed by Warner and then Bancroft.
 “In light of recent events, both Usman and Davey will be rested from our broadcasts over the next few weeks,” Fox Sports managing director Steve Crawley told Australian media. “While we always support all members of our commentary team and welcome a diversity of views which is a feature of our summer of cricket, we also understand the pressure they are under to respond to each and every new comment.
 “We think it is increasingly difficult to focus on the game while the situation continues to unfold and think it is unfair on both commentators to put them in that position. We will continue to monitor the situation.”
 It was unclear when they would return, but Australia play four Tests against New Zealand in December-January after the five-game T20 series that got underway in Melbourne on Saturday.
 Share Updated at  05.47 EST 45m ago 05.43 EST 9th over: Australia 78-2 (Marsh 27, Chaudhary 16) Chaudhary hits successive boundaries off Dawson. If the first shot was good, a firm sweep past short fine leg, then the second was gorgeous: he made room to lift an elegant drive over extra cover.
 At the other end, whether by accident or design, Marsh is playing the anchor role. He has 27 from 25 balls, Chaudhary 16 from 11.
 “Very pleased to have you back on your feet, Mr Smyth. (I have mostly suppressed a memory of my OBO debut 21 years ago, where I rather sniffy informed you the 2005 Ashes series wouldn’t amount to much…),” writes Gervase Greene. “Can I get odds on the likelihood of Mitchell Marsh taking media questions after the game? This might be the first time in recorded history where a winning captain – even if he hits 100 off 50 – declines to be available…”
 May you live in interesting times.
 Share 49m ago 05.39 EST 8th over: Australia 66-2 (Marsh 26, Chaudhary 5) Time for Adil Rashid, who bowled a wicket maiden on this ground in the 2022 T20 World Cup final. He has a short-term point to prove, having been usurped by Liam Dawson in the ODI team, and starts by conceding only four singles from his first over. Good lad.
 Share 52m ago 05.35 EST 7th over: Australia 62-2 (Marsh 24, Chaudhary 3) Marsh humps Will Jacks’ first ball over backward square leg for four. But like Crocombe and Curran earlier in the innings, Jacks recovers well from a first-ball boundary to keep things relatively quiet for the rest of the over.
 Australia need 126 from 78 balls ; the contest is afoot.
 Share 54m ago 05.33 EST 6th over: Australia 53-2 (Marsh 18, Chaudhary 0) “I fully endorse your view that Dawson should’ve had 40 or 50 Test caps to his name by now,” writes James Matthews. “Has it ever been fathomed why the England management has so steadfastly ignored him for a series of spinners with ‘metrics’ and ‘potential’ in their favour, but little else? He has the spinner’s biggest weapon in spades: the ability to draw the batter into a stroke he doesn’t really want to play. England’s Test side has been calling out for a ‘control’ spinner ever since Leach was jettisoned.”
 That probably needs an essay, too, as it’s a complicated case. Lotta ins, lotta outs, lotta what-have-yous. My biggest frustration is that they binned him after one poor performance at Old Trafford last year, a game that bore precisely bugger all resemblance to what was going to happen in Australia. That said, I understand why they invested in Shoaib Bashir given his height and how well he bowled against India in his debut series.
 I promise I’ll get over the 2025-26 Ashes, one of these decades.
 Share 55m ago 05.32 EST WICKET! Australia 53-2 (Harper c Jacks b Crocombe 32)
 Henry Crocombe takes his first T20I wicket. Harper, who uppercut thrillingly for six earlier in the over, blasted a slower ball miles in the air and was taken at point by Jacks. That was a charming cameo on debut from Harper: 32 from 15 balls with three fours and two sixes.
 View image in fullscreen Will Jacks catches out Sam Harper. Photograph: James Ross/EPA Share Updated at  05.39 EST 1h ago 05.27 EST 5th over: Australia 42-1 (Marsh 17, Harper 23) On comes Sam Curran, who loved the MCG dimensions during the 2022 T20 World Cup. Marsh violates his first ball down the ground for four, then survives a Spandex-tight run-out referral after a direct hit from Overton at mid-on.
 England thought it was out; so did Marsh, who took his gloves off and was in the process of doing one when the replay showed he had just made his ground. It’s Shadab Khan all over again.
 Five from the over, a very good comeback from Curran after a boundary first ball.
 “Look, Rob,” begins Ian Copestake, “we know you like a joke as much as a stat about how many pastries the Aussies consumed in the lunch break of the 1984 Test in Adelaide against the Windies. But c’mon, what is Jake Fraser-McGurk’s real name?”
 Erm, Jake Matthew Fraser-McGurk?
 Share 1h ago 05.22 EST 4th over: Australia 37-1 (Marsh 12, Harper 23) Jamie Overton’s first over disappears for 21! Twenty of them came from the bat of the local boy Sam Harper. He edged four, top-edged just short of the diving Donald, slashed a more deliberate four through backwrd point, scooped an outrageous six and then flashed another boundary past the keeper Jordan Cox. Welcome to international cricket.
 View image in fullscreen Sam Harper hits out. Photograph: James Ross/AAP Share Updated at  05.27 EST 1h ago 05.16 EST 3rd over: Australia 16-1 (Marsh 12, Harper 3) Harper works Dawson off the pads for two, his first runs in international cricket. Another good over from Dawson, though – four from it.
 Share 1h ago 05.15 EST 2nd over: Australia 11-1 (Marsh 10, Harper 0) Marsh welcomes Henry Crocombe to T20Is by pulling his first ball over backward square leg for six. Marsh is extraordinarily good on the pull, a shot he played repeatedly during one of the great forgotten innings: 118 from 118 balls at Headingley during the 2023 Ashes. That knock deserves a Phil Walker essay.
 Crocombe holds his nerve, adjusts his line and length, and concedes only three from the last five balls of the over. That’s a good comeback.
 “Substack?” sniffs Ian Copestake. “Bleh. Is like those cameras with phones on them. I mean who wants that?!”
 Share 1h ago 05.10 EST 1st over: Australia 3-1 (Marsh 2, Harper 0) A terrific first over from Dawson. The new batter is the debutant Sam Harper.
 “Didn’t realise you weren’t well,” writes Felix Wood. “Sorry to hear and very glad you’re back on your feet, and selfishly that you’re back on OBO duty. You’re the best in the business.”
 Stop it now. (Don’t stop it. But please do know how touched and grateful I am.)
 Share 1h ago 05.09 EST WICKET! Australia 3-1 (Fraser-McGurk b Dawson 1)
 Canny is as canny does. Dawson sees – or senses – Fraser-McGurk coming down the track, holds the ball back and beats him all ends up. Fraser-McGurk says goodnight to his stumps and keeps walking. Experience 1-0 Youth.
 View image in fullscreen Jake Fraser-McGurk of Australia is bowled by Dawson. Photograph: Quinn Rooney/Getty Images Share Updated at  05.20 EST 1h ago 05.06 EST Liam Dawson , a canny left-arm spinner who should have played 40 Tests including four or five in Australia last winter but let’s not get into that now, will open the bowling.
 Share 1h ago 05.04 EST Time for the runchase. We say it every time, but Mitch Marsh is a key man. He’s opening the batting with Jake Fraser-McGurk.
 Share 1h ago 05.03 EST Hey, I’ve found a great new platform that lets writers, podcasters and video creators share work directly with subscribers. It’s called Substack – that name will never catch on – and I’ll be writing on there about cricket, football and maybe mental health. Please subscribe !
 Share 1h ago 04.59 EST A reminder of the latest sandpaper news 
 Pat Cummins to remain Test captain despite intense pressure amid sandpapergate scandal Read more Share 2h ago 04.49 EST Harry Brook has just given a pair of gloves to a young fan who was hit by one of his sixes. He’s being interviewed by Adam Gilchrist on the TV coverage.
 double quotation mark I feel like we’ve got a good score. Hopefully we can use the dimensions of the ground to our advantage.
 I moved around a lot, mainly to try to put the ball bowlers, but I’m still playing the ball on instinct. I’m literally trying to see the balla and hit the ball.
 Gilly would surely approve of that last line.
 Share 2h ago 04.48 EST Australia need 188 to win
 20th over: England 187-9 (Rashid 0) A fabulous last over from Jack Edwards – no boundaries, one wicket, one bye and only four runs off the bat.
 Cracking fightback from Australia, who were in all sorts when England were 104-2 after eight overs.
 Share 2h ago 04.47 EST WICKET! England 187-9 (Dawson run out 17)
 Dawson is run out off the final delivery after turning for a non-existent second just in case there was a misfield.
 Share 2h ago 04.44 EST WICKET! England 185-8 (Overton b Edwards 2)
 Overton is dropped by Tim David, a very tough low chanve at long-on. That’s at least six chances that have gone down. In thise case, no matter: Edwards cleans him up with a quite beautiful slower yorker. That was nigh-on perfect.
 Two balls remaining.
 View image in fullscreen Overton out, bowled by a yorker from Jack Edwards. Photograph: James Ross/AAP Share Updated at  05.01 EST 2h ago 04.41 EST 19th over: England 181-7 (Dawson 13, Overton 1) The new batter Jamie Overton cloths a hook straight up in the air. Somehow it lands safely.
 The highest successful chase in a T20 international at the MCG is Sri Lanka’s 172 for 5 in 2017.
 “I took my time to be convinced by Jordan Cox, but he’s a gem of a cricketer, isn’t he?” writes James Matthews. “Always bats unselfishly and so often adds impetus towards the end of the batting effort. Him and Jacks in the middle order give England wonderful balance and their big guns up the order licence to go hard at every ball, safe in the knowledge that there is genuine depth right down the order.
 “And as I type, he holes out. I stand by my point, yeronner.”
 Yeah, I was the same. I was think I was spooked when he was bounced out by Alzarri in that ODI series in the Caribbean two years ago, but there is so much to like about him. And batters are allowed to improve against the short ball: contrast Jonny Bairstow v Kemar Roach in 2012 and then v New Zealand in 2022.
 Share Updated at  04.42 EST 2h ago 04.39 EST WICKET! England 180-7 (Cox c Davies b Meredith 27)
 A useful cameo from Cox, 27 from 20 balls, ends with a roundhouse pull that is nicely taken on the run at deep midwicket.
 Australia are facing a record target on this ground, yet they’ve still done well to pull this back. At one stage England were eyeing 250.
 Share 2h ago 04.36 EST 18th over: England 175-6 (Cox 23, Dawson 12) Zampa’s final over goes for 11. First Dawson lifts an elegantly boundary over wide mid-on, then Cox picks the gap to the left of mid- off .
 It would have been 15 from the over had a fierce blow from Cox not hit the non-striker Dawson. Two overs to go.
 “Very glad to hear of your recovery – hope you’re ok,” writes James Brough. “Every so often, you find something that highlights how the game has changed. When I started watching cricket, David Gower was England’s premier batsman. I looked up his career stats for something a few days ago. Test career – 10 sixes in 117 games. Harry Brook just hit six sixes in about 20 minutes...”
 View image in fullscreen Jordan Cox dives to make his ground. Photograph: Asanka Brendon Ratnayake/AP Share Updated at  04.39 EST 2h ago 04.33 EST 17th over: England 164-6 (Cox 18, Dawson 6) Cox survives a run-out referral after turning Davies into the leg side and coming back from a second. He had to scramble desperately to make his ground, but did so successfully. Like vibes, dives matter.
 Cox celebrates his reprieve by dumping a reverse sweep over the top for four.
 “Hi Rob,” says Gary Naylor. “Lovely to have you back. I recognise that feeling you describe with ‘the surge of joie de vivre you get after serious illness’ not through poor health (so far) but from near-misses on the motorbike. The thrill was such that I’d never felt so alive. So, do batters get that same rush after a successful DRS review? Maybe they have enough joie de vivre.”
 Maybe they get it while facing extreme pace? Robin Smith certainly loved the sensation of a 90mph bouncer whooshing past his nose.
 Share 2h ago 04.27 EST 16th over: England 155-6 (Cox 11, Dawson 4) The legspinner Nikhil Chaudhary, playing only his fourth T20 international, finishes a game-changing spell with superb figures of 4-0-21-2. He conceded only one boundary, and even that was a false stroke from Tom Banton.
 Share 2h ago 04.24 EST WICKET! England 150-6 (Curran c Shaw b Chaudhary 21)
 That last entry aged well. Curran slices the first ball of Chaudhary’s final over to Shaw, who takes a good catch running in from the cover boundary.
 Curran goes for 21 from 21 balls; that will annoy him more than a single-figure dismissal.
 View image in fullscreen Australia's Lachie Shaw takes the catch to dismiss Dawson. Photograph: Asanka Brendon Ratnayake/AP Share Updated at  04.28 EST 2h ago 04.23 EST 15th over: England 150-5 (Curran 21, Cox 10) This situation is perfect for Curran, who is a much better T20 player when he has a bit of time to get his eye in. He has 21 from 19 balls, while Cox – who ends Riley Meredith’s over by deflecting a low full toss for four – is 10 from 10.
 Share Updated at  04.23 EST 2h ago 04.18 EST 14th over: England 141-5 (Curran 17, Cox 5) Curran rifles Zampa down the ground for four, the first boundary since the ninth over. Cracking shot. Even after a mid-innings lull, England are scoring at ten an over.
 Share 2h ago 04.15 EST 13th over: England 133-5 (Curran 11, Cox 3) Chaudhary continues the fightback that he started with the wicket of Brook. Six from the over, none in boundaries.
 This has been an innings of three-thirds
 First 3 overs 18-2
